ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In an experiment in which a certain group explores Lenz's law, the group students designed the circuit shown in the figure to carry out the experiment. A fixed coil M is wound around a long straight iron core; the right end of the iron core is in close contact with a wooden cylinder; a closed metal ring N is sleeved on the wooden cylinder, and N can move without friction on the wooden cylinder. M is connected in the circuit shown in the figure, where R is a slide rheostat, E1 and E2 are DC power supplies, and S is a single-pole double-throw switch. Among the following situations, the one in which N can be observed to move to the right is (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In the Lenz's law experiment shown in the question figure, if S was originally open, at the instant when S is closed toward a, in which direction will the closed metal ring N move?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the Lenz's law experiment shown in the question figure, if S was originally open, at the instant when S is closed toward a, in which direction will the closed metal ring N move?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the question figure, on the left is a horizontally placed long iron core, with a fixed coil M wound on it; to the right of the iron core is connected a wooden cylinder, on which a closed metal ring N is sleeved. N is located on the right side of coil M and can move left and right along the horizontal direction. In the circuit below there are a slide rheostat R, DC power supplies E1 and E2, and a single-pole double-throw switch S; contact a is at the upper right, and contact b is at the lower right. The question states that S was originally open, and now S is closed toward a, that is, the branch where E1 is located energizes coil M. Reasoning: at the instant when S is closed toward a, the current in coil M goes from none to present, so the magnetic flux passing through the closed metal ring N near the right end of the iron core suddenly increases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field formed by the induced current generated in N must hinder this increase in magnetic flux. Viewed equivalently, the face of N close to M will form the same magnetic pole as the right end of coil M, so M and N repel each other. Since N is on the right side of M, after being repelled it will move away from M, so N moves to the right.
